page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on KVM virtualization. The server utilizes an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, providing 16 vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 128 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio tailored for high-memory requirements. Hardware features include support for AVX-512, AES cryptography, and FMA instruction sets. The instance includes no local storage drives and relies entirely on external network-attached volumes, while providing a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance assessments highlight average multi-core capabilities paired with lower single-threaded efficiency. Single-core benchmarks, including single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests, score in lower percentiles due to the moderate 2.5 GHz clock frequency. Conversely, multi-threaded evaluations such as multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and software compilation tests perform in the middle percentile tier. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth tests yield typical throughput figures, supporting high-concurrency key-value store operations such as Redis at 11.3 million operations per second.

Regarding cost efficiency, the ecs.se1.4xlarge provides high memory allocation relative to core count without requiring investment in specialized high-frequency compute hardware. Primary tradeoffs include lower per-core execution speeds and a lack of integrated local storage. This profile is suited for memory-intensive applications that tolerate standard single-core speeds, such as in-memory caches, relational databases, multi-threaded processing pipelines, and static web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on KVM hyperthreading architecture, it provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, paired with 128 GB of system memory for an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance features no local disk storage, relying on external block storage, and operates with a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPU hardware. Performance metrics show average multi-core processing power and memory bandwidth alongside weaker single-threaded performance. This hardware profile provides resource efficiency for memory-heavy workloads that do not demand peak per-core compute speeds. Recommended workloads include in-memory key-value stores like Redis, relational databases, web serving, and concurrent multi-threaded data processing tasks.
